title: C482 — Right-hand rear side marker lamp connector
introduction:
I use this sheet to follow the rear marker lamp's paper trail: connector identity, harness drawing, cavity rows and service-pigtail reference. The cavity labels are the useful handoff between the picture and the table; a similar-looking housing alone cannot tell the whole story.

The right-hand lamp description and left-side ground wording refer to different parts of the circuit's geography. Preserve both without guessing the wire route or exact ground attachment. This page covers reference reading; physical access, viewing direction, test conditions and repairs need their own procedures. Gauge conventions and Box, Size and Used codes remain undefined here.

edits.why: The associated illustration has a rounded outer housing, an upper rectangular feature and side-by-side cavity labels. I use that printed outline to recognize the view, then match the labels to their rows. The harness entry ties the drawing to this reference without establishing where to reach the connector or how its retaining features move.

Read across each cavity row to keep its circuit identifier, wire-color code, gauge entry, function and terminal reference together. The functions distinguish the ground return from the park-lamp relay circuit. Preserve the full ground-location wording as a reference label; it is not an attachment-location illustration. A relay label describes an electrically switched circuit without identifying a separate plug-in relay, and neither row establishes that the circuit works.

Match the kit entry in the identification table to the service-parts row, where the service identifier and engineering shell are separate fields. Keep the service assembly's gauge and material entries with that assembly rather than applying them to the original circuit wires. The named image file is a catalog pointer. These details support identification but do not supply a splice, terminal-replacement or installation method.
